C0.quote: justification for a given choice in the context of a given corpus
C0.note: Justifying outcomes of voting rules via axioms; axiomatic/computational aspects of voting.

C1.quote: we develop a definition of the notion of justification
C1.note: Main results: conceptual definition of justification (OT), Theorem 1 coherence (AX), encoding/MUS algorithm (AL), exhaustive computational experiment on 3 agents/3 alternatives (not real data nor sampled simulation, so not coded SI/EM). Primary AL by number of results; borderline with OT.

C2.1.quote: Given such a profile of individual preferences

C2.2.quote: set of all strict linear orders on X

C2.3.quote: They each have their own subjective preferences over the set

C2.4.note: Preferences are the rule's input, described alternately as preferences, declared and reported preferences, with a single notation; no statement of sincerity or of a gap.

C3.1.note: No strategic misreporting analysed; strategyproofness only mentioned in passing as a hard axiom.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost or distortion notion used.

C5.1.note: Pareto and Condorcet appear only as axioms used in explanations; no results about welfare or efficiency of outcomes.

VOT.quote_behav: A profile for an electorate N declaring preferences is a function
VOT.note: Agents appear only as given preference inputs; fixed by the model.

ORG.note: Committee in Example 1 is an illustration, not an agent of the model.

OTH.note: Audience of the justification, whose interests/acceptance of axioms are discussed; behaviour not modelled.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED type.

claims.quote: we may use justifications to defend a decision already taken
to serve as a stand-in when no specific voting rule seems acceptable
we can use this approach in lieu of a voting rule

C9.1.note: Claims about use in real decision settings and on which rule/approach to use.

C9.2.quote: publish all ballots received (in anonymised form)
C9.2.note: Examples involve real ballots/elections, but relation between ballots and held preferences, and that voters are non-strategic, is not stated; axioms-as-norms acceptable to audience is stated.
